learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of legacy configuration and plugin directives.
Apply one appropriate technique to a small Tailwind CSS example.

content.intro: In this lesson, focus on legacy configuration and plugin directives and connect it to the way Tailwind CSS generates and applies utility styles.
content.why_it_matters: Legacy Configuration and Plugin Directives helps a team reuse visual decisions without losing flexibility for real application interfaces.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum highlights: Understanding the v3 JavaScript configuration model; Loading a legacy configuration with @config where applicable; Loading compatible legacy plugins with @plugin; Recognizing deprecated or changed options; Planning gradual migrations to CSS-first configuration. Treat these as practical decisions rather than a list to memorize: identify the intended behavior, choose the smallest suitable utility or directive, and inspect what the browser receives.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Legacy Configuration and Plugin Directives

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with the example, change one decision related to legacy configuration and plugin directives, then compare the outcome. In a Tailwind-enabled project, confirm the generated CSS exists; class strings alone do not make styles available without a configured build.

content_blocks.title: Version and compatibility note
content_blocks.text: This course prioritizes Tailwind CSS v4. Confirm your installed version and use its matching official guide. Snippets using v3 directives or configuration are labelled as legacy and should not be mixed blindly with v4 syntax.

content.task: Create a minimal example demonstrating legacy configuration and plugin directives. Include a before/after comparison and explain why the chosen utility, variant or directive is appropriate.
task_acceptance_criteria: Demonstrate at least one decision tied to legacy configuration and plugin directives.
Keep the example easy to inspect, with complete utility names.
Test the outcome and document one limitation or environment assumption.
hints: Identify which listed syllabus topic is most important to legacy configuration and plugin directives.
Change one utility, token, variant or configuration setting at a time.
Inspect generated CSS and computed styles before changing unrelated code.
content.expected_output: A theme variable defines a brand color; a configured build makes the matching utility available.
troubleshooting: If no style appears, verify the package, CSS import and build-tool integration before changing the HTML.
If only a state or breakpoint style fails, check the full class token, source detection, condition and computed CSS.
For a framework snippet, import the stylesheet through its supported entry point and consult the current official guide.
common_mistakes: Applying legacy configuration and plugin directives without checking generated styles or browser behavior.
Mixing Tailwind v3 and v4 setup examples without a migration plan.
Treating visual appearance as a substitute for semantic markup, keyboard usability or actual component behavior.
summary: Legacy Configuration and Plugin Directives is one part of a predictable utility-first styling workflow.
Keep examples small, test the built interface and use version-matched documentation.
